events.text: Possible conquest of Babylon against Egypt where Babylon received a compensation through the Egypt’s wealth. (Eze 29:18-20; 30:10-12.) One Babylonian text, dated to Nebuchadnezzar’s 37th year, mentions a campaign against Egypt. Whether it relates to the original conquest or merely to a subsequent military action cannot be said.

events.text: Babylonian king Evil-merodach succeeded Nebuchadnezzar to the throne. Evil-merodach extended kindness to Jehoiachin the king of Judah by releasing him from the house of detention. Evil-merodach granted him a position of favor above all the other kings who were in captivity in Babylon. (2Ki 25:27-30; Jer 52:31-34)

events.text: On December this year, A pagan altar was built over the great altar of Jehovah at Jerusalem’s temple, and sacrifices were offered on it to the Olympian Zeus, by Seleucid King Antiochus IV (Epiphanes). Shocked but courageous men of the countryside banded together under the leadership of Judas Maccabaeus and waged bitter warfare until they gained possession of Jerusalem. This starts the Hasmonian dynasty.

events.text: On September this year, an important decree was issued in Jerusalem confirming that Simon Maccabee was appointed as leader and a high priest. This appointment was done politically. He was careful by not using the title as a ‘king’ but ‘a leader of the people’.

events.text: The Seleucid dynasty lost a crucial battle with the Parthians. This gives way to John Hyrcanus, son of Simon Maccabee to “able to recover in full Judea’s political independence and to begin expanding in various directions.”
events.title: The Seleucid dynasty lost a crucial battle with the Parthians

events.text: Alexander Jannaeus, son of John Hyrcanus, started to rule and later declared himself both high priest and king. The conflicts between the Hasmonaeans and the Pharisees intensified, even leading to a civil war in which 50,000 Jews perished.

events.text: Salome Alexandra, wife of Alexander Jannaeus, became the successor of Jannaeus’ kingdom. The Pharisees were restored to positions of authority, and the laws against their religious ordinances were revoked.

events.title: Roman General Pompey dethroned Antiochus XIII of the Seleucid dynasty

events.text: Salome’s sons, Hyrcanus II and Aristobulus II entered a power struggle. Both lacked the political and military insight of their forefathers, and it seems that neither understood the full significance of the increasing Roman presence in the area. They turned to the Roman ruler Pompey while he was in Damascus and requested his mediation in their dispute.

events.text: Rome became the sixth world power, and rules Jerusalem (John 19:15; Rev. 17:10) Pompey and his troops marched into Jerusalem and took control. It was the beginning of the end for the Hasmonaean dynasty.
